mtp.connectedToast.title: Connected to {deviceName}

@mtp.connectedToast.title.description: Title of the toast shown when an Android/Kindle/camera device connects over USB.

placeholders.deviceName: the connected device's display name (for example Pixel 7), or a generic fallback

mtp.connectedToast.body: {platform, select, macos {Cmdr paused the macOS camera daemon (ptpcamerad) to access this device. To use it in another app, disable MTP support in settings.} windows {} other {To use this device in another app, disable MTP support in settings.}}

@mtp.connectedToast.body.description: Body of the device-connected toast. The macos branch explains that Cmdr paused the system camera daemon and how to release the device; the other branch (Linux) only says how to release it. The windows branch is empty on purpose (Windows shares the device with File Explorer, so the toast has no body line there): keep it empty. ptpcamerad is a macOS system process name; keep it literal. MTP is a device-transfer protocol acronym; keep it. The screenshot shows the macOS wording.

@mtp.connectedToast.dontShowAgain.description: Checkbox label that suppresses the device-connected toast for future connections.

@mtp.connectedToast.disableMtp.description: Button that turns off MTP device support entirely. The ellipsis hints further confirmation/settings. MTP is a protocol acronym; keep it. Tight mini button.

@mtp.connectedToast.ok.description: Button that acknowledges and dismisses the device-connected toast. Tight mini button.

mtp.permissionDialog.title: Can’t access USB device

@mtp.permissionDialog.title.description: Title of the Linux dialog shown when Cmdr lacks permission to access a connected USB (MTP) device.

mtp.permissionDialog.description: Cmdr doesn’t have permission to access this device. Linux needs udev rules to grant MTP device access.

@mtp.permissionDialog.description.description: Main explanation in the Linux USB-permission dialog. udev is a Linux device-management term and MTP a protocol acronym; keep both literal.

mtp.permissionDialog.explanation: Run this command in your terminal to install the rules and reload them:

@mtp.permissionDialog.explanation.description: Instruction above the copyable terminal command in the Linux USB-permission dialog.

mtp.permissionDialog.helpText: After running the command, unplug and replug the device, then retry.

@mtp.permissionDialog.helpText.description: Follow-up instruction below the command in the Linux USB-permission dialog, telling the user to reconnect the device and retry.

@mtp.permissionDialog.close.description: Button that closes the Linux USB-permission dialog without retrying.

@mtp.permissionDialog.retry.description: Button that retries connecting to the USB device after the user installed the udev rules.

mtp.ptpcameradDialog.title: Can’t connect to MTP device

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.title.description: Title of the dialog shown, on every OS, when another process holds a connected MTP device so Cmdr can't open it. MTP is a protocol acronym; keep it.

mtp.ptpcameradDialog.inUseBy: The device is in use by <processName>{process}</processName>.

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.inUseBy.description: Sentence naming which process currently holds the device. <processName> wraps the process name and renders it emphasized (bold).

placeholders.process: the blocking process description (for example pid 45145, ptpcamerad)

mtp.ptpcameradDialog.inUseGeneric: Another process has exclusive access to the device.

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.inUseGeneric.description: First sentence of the MTP-conflict dialog when the blocking process can't be named: the fallback on macOS, and what Windows and Linux always read.

mtp.ptpcameradDialog.explanation: {platform, select, macos {On macOS, the system daemon ptpcamerad automatically claims Android devices. To work around this, run the following command in Terminal (keep it running while using Cmdr):} windows {Another app is holding the phone, and it has to let go before Cmdr can connect.} other {Only one app can talk to a phone over MTP at a time, and your desktop usually mounts a phone as soon as it’s plugged in.}}

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.explanation.description: Explanation in the MTP-conflict dialog, why another process holds the phone. The macos branch: the system camera daemon grabs Android devices, so a workaround command (shown below it) must run. The windows branch: some other app holds the phone. The other branch (Linux): the desktop's own phone support mounted it, and MTP serves one app at a time. <code> (macos branch only) wraps the process name in monospace styling. ptpcamerad is a macOS process name; keep it literal. "Terminal" is Apple's app: use the name your language's macOS shows for it (most keep the English name, Chinese doesn't; check the reference pile or the app bundle).

mtp.ptpcameradDialog.helpText: {platform, select, macos {This command continuously stops ptpcamerad while running. Press <key>Ctrl+C</key> in Terminal to stop it when done.} windows {Close the app that’s using the phone, then retry.} other {Unmount the phone in your file manager, then retry.}}

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.helpText.description: Last line of the MTP-conflict dialog, above its Close and Retry connection buttons. The macos branch sits under the workaround command and explains how to stop it. The windows and other (Linux) branches have no command above them and say what to do before retrying; "file manager" is the desktop's own file browser. <key> (macos branch only) wraps the keyboard-key pill for Ctrl+C (a styled chip). ptpcamerad is a process name; keep it literal. "Terminal" is Apple's app: use the name your language's macOS shows for it (most keep the English name, Chinese doesn't; check the reference pile or the app bundle).

placeholders.key: wraps the inline Ctrl+C key pill; keep the wrapper, the key glyph is filled in by the app

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.close.description: Button that closes the MTP-conflict dialog without retrying.

@mtp.ptpcameradDialog.retry.description: Button that retries connecting to the MTP device after the user freed it (on macOS, by running the workaround command).

mtp.readiness.connecting: Still connecting. Unlock your phone and tap Allow if it asks.

@mtp.readiness.connecting.description: One line under a phone's greyed-out row in the volume switcher (the dropdown listing disks and devices) while Cmdr keeps retrying to open the phone. Says what the user can do. ❗ Keep the condition ("if it asks"): the phone may be showing no prompt at all, so this must never read as though one is on screen. "Allow" is the button on ANDROID's own prompts: render it exactly as Android's own translation of that button reads in your language.
@mtp.readiness.connecting.screenshotNote: MTP (phone/camera) device messaging: a connect/permission dialog or toast tied to an MTP device. This shows the MTP browse surface for context. Keep device/protocol names (MTP, PTP) as-is.

mtp.readiness.connectingTooltip: Cmdr keeps trying while your phone stays plugged in, and you can open it once it connects.

@mtp.readiness.connectingTooltip.description: Hover tooltip on that same greyed-out row. Says why the row can't be opened yet and that nothing else is needed: retrying is automatic and goes on until the phone is unplugged. "Cmdr" is the product name; "it" is the phone.
@mtp.readiness.connectingTooltip.screenshotNote: MTP (phone/camera) device messaging: a connect/permission dialog or toast tied to an MTP device. This shows the MTP browse surface for context. Keep device/protocol names (MTP, PTP) as-is.

@mtp.deviceFallbackName.description: Generic fallback name for a connected MTP device when its real display name isn't known yet. MTP is a protocol acronym; keep it.
@mtp.deviceFallbackName.screenshotNote: MTP (phone/camera) device messaging: a connect/permission dialog or toast tied to an MTP device. This shows the MTP browse surface for context. Keep device/protocol names (MTP, PTP) as-is.
